recognize_zh: 中央四顆緊貼的紅系前驅細胞：下方為細顆粒染色質、深藍細胞質的早期細胞，右側大細胞染色質已呈粗塊但核仍大，展示同一視野內不同成熟階段且細胞偏大；左側有破碎的網狀細胞殘骸，背景為卵圓形與淚滴形紅血球，符合巨母紅血球性貧血。
features: Cluster of four erythroid precursors at different maturation stages
Early basophilic precursor with finely stippled chromatin and deep blue cytoplasm (bottom)
Large later-stage erythroblast with coarsely clumped chromatin but persistently large nucleus (right), indicating asynchrony
Smaller basophilic and polychromatic precursors (left and top)
Smeared fibrillar cellular debris at left; small dense nucleated cell at top right
Background oval macrocytes and teardrop cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cluster of erythroid precursors spanning early basophilic to later polychromatic stages. The cells are enlarged, and the more mature erythroblast retains a large nucleus with partially condensed chromatin while its cytoplasm is hemoglobinizing, indicating nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony. A smeared cell with fibrillar debris lies at the left, and the background shows oval macrocytes and teardrop cells. The findings are consistent with megaloblastic erythropoiesis in B12/folate deficiency.

ddx.vs: MDS may show megaloblastoid erythroblasts but also nuclear budding, internuclear bridging, ring sideroblasts and clonal cytogenetics with normal vitamin levels.
Normoblastic precursors decrease in size synchronously with chromatin condensation and lack the giant, open-chromatin forms seen here.
Drug-induced megaloblastosis is morphologically identical and is distinguished by medication history with normal B12/folate levels.
